n: A new message introduces another acted-out sign.

f.w: The word of the LORD also came unto me

n: Ezekiel lives among people who have eyes and ears but refuse to see or hear spiritual truth. Isaiah, Jeremiah, and Jesus used the same image.

f.w: which have eyes to see, and see not

n: He must pack an exile’s bag in broad daylight and move from place to place while people watch. Perhaps the drama will make them think.

f.w: stuff for removing
f.g: Baggage for exile—the few things a deportee could carry.

f.w: it may be they will consider
f.g: God still hopes they will reflect and repent.

n: He sets his bag out by day and leaves in the evening like someone being marched off as a captive.

f.w: at even

n: He must dig through the wall of his house—mud brick in Babylon—and carry his belongings out through the hole.

f.w: Dig thou through the wall
f.g: Babylonian houses were mud brick, easy to dig through.

n: He carries the bag on his shoulder at dusk with his face covered so he cannot see the ground. Ezekiel himself is God’s sign to Israel.

f.w: thou shalt cover thy face
f.g: A detail pointing to a blinded king (v. 13).

f.w: a sign

n: Ezekiel obeys every detail. A prophet’s obedience is part of his message.

f.w: I did so as I was commanded

n: The next morning the Lord explains the sign.

f.w: in the morning
f.g: After the people had watched the night’s performance.

n: The people had asked, “What are you doing?” His strange actions got their attention.

f.w: What doest thou?

n: The message concerns the “prince” in Jerusalem—King Zedekiah—and all Israel there.

f.w: burden
f.g: A prophetic oracle; also a pun on the bag Ezekiel carried.

f.w: the prince
f.g: Ezekiel calls Zedekiah “prince,” perhaps because many still regarded the exiled Jehoiachin as the true king.

n: “I am your sign”: just as Ezekiel acted it out, the people of Jerusalem will be carried off into captivity.

f.w: I am your sign

n: Zedekiah will try to escape at night through a hole in the wall, carrying his things, his face covered. This happened exactly when Jerusalem fell: the king fled by night through a gap in the wall.

f.w: the prince that is among them shall bear upon his shoulder in the twilight

n: A striking prophecy: Zedekiah will be taken to Babylon yet will not see it, though he dies there. It was fulfilled when the Babylonians blinded him before taking him to Babylon.

f.w: yet shall he not see it, though he shall die there
My net also will I spread upon him

n: His bodyguards and troops will be scattered, and the sword will pursue them.

f.w: all his bands

n: Scattered among the nations, they will finally recognize the Lord.

f.w: disperse them in the countries

n: God will spare a few survivors so that, among the nations, they can testify that Israel’s fall was due to its own sins and not to God’s weakness.

f.w: that they may declare all their abominations among the heathen

n: Another message and another sign.

f.w: Moreover the word of the LORD came to me

n: Ezekiel must eat and drink while shaking with fear, acting out the terror of the coming siege.

f.w: with quaking
carefulness

n: Jerusalem’s people will eat and drink with anxiety and horror because their land will be stripped bare, all because of the violence of its people.

f.w: astonishment
because of the violence of all them that dwell therein

n: Populated towns will become ruins and the land a wasteland.

f.w: the cities that are inhabited shall be laid waste

n: Another message, this time answering a popular saying.

f.w: the word of the LORD came unto me

n: People had a proverb: “Time goes on and every vision comes to nothing.” Because predicted judgment hadn’t happened yet, they assumed it never would.

f.w: The days are prolonged, and every vision faileth

n: God will put an end to that proverb. The new one will be: “The days are near, and every vision will be fulfilled.”

f.w: the effect of every vision

n: False visions and flattering fortune-telling will cease in Israel.

f.w: flattering divination
f.g: Smooth, comforting predictions people wanted to hear.

n: God declares that what he says will happen—no more delay. It will come in their own lifetime.

f.w: the word that I shall speak shall come to pass

n: Another message responds to a second excuse.

f.w: Again the word of the LORD came to me

n: Others admitted the prophecies might be true but said they were about the distant future, not them. It was a way of avoiding personal repentance.

f.w: he prophesieth of the times that are far off

n: God replies: none of his words will be delayed any longer. What he has spoken will be done. Within six years Jerusalem fell.

f.w: There shall none of my words be prolonged any more
